arm: self-verification — denali's own claims, checked with denali's own tool
status: POST-HOC. Not pre-registered. Reports whatever came back.
the_uncomfortable_part: Our own screen is the only one here that clears its null, and that is NOT evidence that our screen is better science. It is a structural property of the mapping: our hits count perturbations over ~9,800 knockdowns, so set size gets no arithmetic head start and the null sits near zero. The seven external screens are classical overlap enrichment, where hits are counted over each set's own members and the no-biology value is large by construction. We are comparing our own data against an easier baseline than theirs, and a reader should discount the contrast accordingly. Reported because a verification tool that flatters its author is worth nothing.
what_this_does_not_show: Nothing about the quality, correctness or reliability of any study whose table appears here. A ranking indistinguishable from its own null is not a wrong result; it is a ranking this particular measure cannot resolve. No study is named as a finding and none is criticised.
scope: Collection-level only. No gene, gene set, publication or author is named as a finding. No clinical or wet-lab claim follows.

full.claim_as_stated: Set size alone explains 46.5% of the variance in this screen's gene-set hit ranking.

not_verifiable.what: the biology of any set in the ranking
not_verifiable.why: this tool reads only set sizes and hit counts; it never sees a gene, an effect size, or an experiment

not_verifiable.what: read depth, guide efficacy, batch and replicate structure
not_verifiable.why: these are other ways a ranking can be carried by how it was measured, and this tool tests none of them

not_verifiable.what: whether the study's conclusion is correct
not_verifiable.why: a ranking is one line of evidence in a paper and usually not the load-bearing one

mapping.why: hit counts here are not bounded by set size, so hits are counted over some other universe than the set's own members. Size has no arithmetic head start.

full.ranking_verdict: MORE SIZE-CARRIED THAN ITS OWN NULL
full.reading: This ranking is predicted by set size more than a version of itself containing no biology would be: R^2 0.4649 against a null of 0.0182 (95% interval 0.0-0.0981). That means the size relationship here is not merely arithmetic. It does NOT mean the ranking is biologically right -- being distinguishable from a trivial baseline is the lowest bar there is, not a high one.
full.delta_reading: The source states 0.4649; this table measures 0.4649. Difference +0.0000. A difference is not necessarily a discrepancy -- estimands differ, and the source may be computing something adjacent on different rows.
to_make_checkable: state the set size and the count of significant members for every set, not only the significant ones
state the significance threshold that produced the hit counts
state whether hit counts are over each set's own members or over a larger universe -- the correct no-biology null differs and so does the reading
report the size share of the ranking alongside the ranking, so a reader can compare like with like without recomputing it
full.symmetry: Every number above is reproducible by the party being verified, from the same file, with the command above. Nothing was uploaded and nothing left this machine.
full.what_this_is_not: Not a rating of a paper, a laboratory, a company or a person, and not an allegation of any kind. It compares one ranking against a baseline computed from that same ranking's own construction. It names no gene and no gene set, and it nominates nothing.
